name: Amazon Design System
summary: Dense e-commerce UI system built around Amazon Yellow CTAs, Ember typography, and tight product-tile information density.
description: A production-grade prompt for building Amazon's storefront design language: yellow-orange commerce CTAs, deep navy chrome, gold star ratings, and prices engineered to dominate the eye.

whatYouGet: A full commerce color system anchored on the #FF9900 CTA yellow, deep navy #131921 chrome, and semantic reds/greens for deals and stock states
Component specs for product tiles, PDP price blocks, quantity steppers, and lightning-deal countdown banners at exact padding/radius values
House rules that keep every product card scannable at a glance without losing the shopping-list density that defines the brand
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer who specializes in high-conversion e-commerce interfaces. You have shipped storefront apps at scale and understand how commerce UI trades whitespace for decision-enabling density, and how a single disciplined CTA color builds muscle-memory trust across millions of purchase taps.

</role>
<reference_data>
Color roles:
- CTA Yellow #FF9900 (primary Add to Cart / Buy button fill, paired with black #0F1111 text, never white text)
- Yellow Pressed #E68A00, Yellow Highlight #FCD200 (1pt top-edge highlight on CTA buttons)
- Buy Now Orange #F08804 (deeper, reserved for single-click purchase / checkout)
- Deep Navy #131921 (top nav chrome), Secondary Navy #232F3E (sub-nav / deliver-to strip)
- Canvas White #FFFFFF, Surface Muted #F3F3F3, Divider #DDDDDD, Border Default #D5D9D9
- Text Primary #0F1111, Text Secondary #565959, Text Tertiary #848A8C
- Price Red #B12704 (strikethroughs, deal banners), Alert Red #CC0C39 (errors, cart badge)
- Success Green #007600 (delivery-date promises), Prime Teal #007185 (badge/links), Prime Sky #00A8E1 (prime wordmark), Rating Gold #FFA41C (star glyphs)

Typography: Amazon Ember (fallback -apple-system/SF Pro/Segoe UI/Roboto). Weight ladder is strictly 300/400/500/700 — no thin, no black, no italics. Prices are always 700 weight, ranging 16-28pt; hero prices use superscript cents at 14pt against a 28pt dollar figure. Product titles clamp to exactly two lines at 15-16pt/400. Rating counts render at 13pt in the teal link color.

Spacing/radius: 4pt base unit (scale 4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/48). Buttons and inputs use 8pt corner radius — never a full pill except filter chips at 20pt. Product images get 4pt radius; modal sheets 12pt. Standard content margin is 16pt; grid gaps run 12pt with an intentionally tight 8pt row gap in list views.

Distinctive patterns: superscript-cents hero pricing; the two-tone search bar (white field + yellow mic/barcode square, only the trailing corners rounded); the five-piece product-tile bundle (photo, 2-line title, star-rating row, price-with-strikethrough, Prime+delivery line) that must always appear together; the Lightning Deal countdown banner with a live-updating timer; the quantity stepper as a bordered three-segment strip.
</reference_data>
<house_rules>
1. The CTA yellow (#FF9900) always carries black text, never white — this specific contrast pairing is the single most recognizable signal in the app and must never be swapped for a "more accessible-looking" white-on-yellow.
2. Never introduce a second CTA color. Buy Now orange (#F08804) is a deliberately close but distinct shade used only for single-click purchase — it is not a designer's free choice, it is a fixed second tone.
3. Every price renders at weight 700 minimum 16pt — money is never displayed in a light or regular weight anywhere in the interface.
4. Product tiles must show all five data points simultaneously (image, title, rating, price, delivery promise) — collapsing any one of them for "cleaner" design breaks the shopping decision model this UI exists to serve.
5. Rating stars are gold (#FFA41C), categorically distinct from the CTA yellow — do not let them collapse into the same hex value even though both read as "yellow-ish" at a glance.
6. Corner radii stay functional: 8pt on buttons/inputs signals "utility tool," not a rounded, friendly consumer app — resist the urge to soften radii above 12pt except on pill-shaped filter chips.
7. The top nav is always deep navy with a light search field inset inside it — never invert this (a white nav bar with a colored search field breaks the established chrome hierarchy).
      
8. Keep shadows almost entirely absent; the only intentional elevation cue is the 1pt yellow top-highlight on primary CTA buttons, a vestigial 3D affordance that must be preserved even in a flat redesign.
9. Dense list rows use an 8pt vertical gap, tighter than typical iOS list rhythm — resist the instinct to open this up, since density is the functional promise of the surface.
</house_rules>
<the_project>
- App/brand name: [your app name]
- Primary catalog type: [e.g. grocery, electronics, handmade goods]
- Primary CTA verb: [Add to Cart / Reserve / Book, etc.]
- Whether a membership/loyalty badge exists: [yes/no, name it]
- Delivery or fulfillment promise to surface: [e.g. "Ships in 2 days"]
- Platform target: [iOS SwiftUI / React Native / Web]
- Existing brand color constraints, if any: [hex codes or "none"]
- Dark mode required: [yes/no]
</the_project>
<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete color token set (light + dark) mapped to CTA, chrome, semantic (deal/stock/rating), and text roles, each with a one-line usage note.
2. A typography ladder specifying font, size, weight, and line-height for hero price, card price, product title, section title, and metadata — money always at weight 700.
3. Full component specs for the primary CTA button, the product grid tile, and the quantity stepper, each with exact padding, corner radius, and pressed-state values.
4. A PDP (product detail) price-block layout showing hero price with superscript cents, strikethrough original price, and the delivery-promise line.
5. A top-nav + search-bar spec matching the two-tone (chrome + inset search field) pattern, including the mic/scan CTA square.
6. A short do/don't list specific to this project's brand constraints, modeled on "CTA color is singular and never swapped."
7. Three to five ready-to-paste SwiftUI (or your target framework) component snippets implementing the above.
</what_to_give_me>

Run it in Claude or your AI assistant of choice
Paste the generated SwiftUI tokens/components into your project and adjust to your actual brand constraints

name: Cal AI Design System
summary: Dark, OLED-black calorie-tracker system with tabular numerals, an AI capture flow, and a desaturated three-macro accent palette.
description: A production-grade prompt for building Cal AI's near-black, photo-forward nutrition tracker language, with its signature scan-to-log AI flow and calm pastel macro accents.

whatYouGet: A near-black OLED color system with three desaturated macro accents (protein/carbs/fat) and no alarm-red anywhere
Specs for the AI capture flow — reticle viewfinder, processing shimmer, and editable detection-result card — plus the macro ring and hero calorie numeral
House rules covering tabular-numeral discipline, surface-contrast elevation instead of shadows, and the single white-glow capture button
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in health and quantified-self applications, with deep experience building dark-canvas, data-forward interfaces where large numerals and photography carry the emotional weight instead of illustration or copy.

</role>
<reference_data>
Color roles: Canvas Black #0A0A0A (near-black, deliberately not pure #000 for OLED comfort), Elevated Surface #151515, Surface 2 #1E1E1E, Surface 3 #2A2A2A, Divider #252525. Text: Primary #FFFFFF, Secondary #A1A1A1, Tertiary #6E6E6E. Macro accent trio (the entire chromatic story): Protein Blue #4DA8FF, Carbs Amber #FFB54C, Fat Pink #FF6E87 — all deliberately desaturated pastels, never primary-saturated. Action/CTA is white fill #FFFFFF with black #000000 text (not a saturated brand color). Success #42E17D, over-budget state uses the same soft Carbs Amber #FFB54C rather than an alarm red, Destructive #FF5A5A, AI accent Info Indigo #8B8DF5. AI-surface treatment: a subtle two-stop dark gradient wash and a three-stop animated gradient line (#4DA8FF → #8B8DF5 → #FF6E87) during processing.

Typography: a single geometric sans (Inter, or SF Pro Display as fallback) used at every size from 12pt captions up to 72pt hero numerals — no separate display face. Tabular/monospaced-figure numerals are mandatory on every calorie, macro, and timestamp value to stop digits from jittering the layout as they update. Weight floor is 400 (regular) — nothing lighter survives against the dark canvas. Large numerals carry negative tracking (-0.8 to -1.5pt) for density.

Spacing/radius: 4pt base scale (4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/52/68). Card padding is 16pt standard, 24pt for the hero card. Radius scale: 14pt inputs, 16pt small thumbnails, 20pt standard cards, 24pt hero card, 28pt pill CTAs, 50% circles for avatars/rings/capture button.

Distinctive patterns: a bottom-center capture FAB (68pt circle) raised above the tab bar with a soft white glow shadow — the one deliberate "light source" in an otherwise flat, shadow-free UI; a four-corner animated camera reticle; macro progress rings (80pt hero / 64pt compact, 6pt stroke, rounded caps) with tabular value + unit centered inside; meal cards where the food photo bleeds edge-to-edge across the top 60% of the card.
</reference_data>
<house_rules>
1. The canvas is #0A0A0A, not #000000 and not any warmer near-black — this specific near-black is load-bearing for how the app reads on OLED without looking harsh.
2. Never use alarm red for an over-goal or over-budget state — the product's entire emotional register avoids anxiety-inducing color, so over-budget stays in the same soft amber used for carbs.
3. Every numeric value (calories, macros, weights, timestamps) must use tabular/monospaced figures — a proportional-figure number that shifts layout on update is a defect, not a stylistic choice.
4. Elevation comes from surface-color steps (canvas → #151515 → #1E1E1E → #2A2A2A), never from drop shadows — the one deliberate exception is the white capture button's glow, which functions as a light source rather than a shadow.
5. The macro trio is the entire chromatic palette outside of white/success/destructive — do not add a fourth accent color under any circumstance, and never saturate the pastel trio toward primary red/blue/yellow.
6. Big numerals render in the same sans as UI type at heavier weight — never substitute a rounded or friendly display face; the numbers must read as data, not as a mascot's speech bubble.
7. Food photography bleeds to the edges of its card region with no internal margin — the photo is the content, and the card exists to frame it, not to contain it with padding.
8. Motion stays subtle: springs use damping of 0.7 or higher, no overshoot beyond a gentle bounce, and there are no confetti or mascot celebration animations anywhere in the product.
9. The AI-detection processing state gets the signature tri-stop gradient sweep (blue→indigo→pink) — this is the one moment allowed to use all three accents at once, signaling "the model is thinking."
</house_rules>
<the_project>
- App/brand name: [your app name]
- Primary tracked metric(s): [calories, macros, water, other]
- AI capture input: [camera scan / barcode / manual entry / all three]
- Number of accent categories needed: [e.g. 3 macros, or a different count]
- Streak or gamification mechanic: [yes/no, describe]
- Platform target: [iOS SwiftUI / React Native / Web]
- Light mode required as a real parity mode or a rare fallback: [specify]
- Existing brand constraints: [hex codes or "none"]
</the_project>
<what_to_give_me>
1. A full dark-mode-first color token set (canvas, surface steps, macro/category accents, semantic states) with usage notes for each.
2. A typography ladder from hero numeral down to caption, specifying that all numeric roles use tabular figures.
3. Component specs for the hero "today" summary card, the macro/category progress ring, and the primary meal/entry card with photo bleed.
4. A full spec for the AI capture flow: viewfinder reticle, processing overlay with the gradient shimmer, and the editable AI-detection result card.
5. The capture FAB spec, including its glow shadow and position relative to the tab bar.
6. A short do/don't list grounded in "no alarm colors, no mascots, tabular numerals only."
7. Three to five ready-to-paste SwiftUI (or your target framework) component snippets implementing the above.
</what_to_give_me>

name: Character.AI Design System
summary: Near-black persona-chat system defined by tucked-corner asymmetric bubbles, italic roleplay narration, and one rationed accent blue.
description: A production-grade prompt for building Character.AI's immersive persona-chat language: calm grey bubbles differentiated by a single tucked corner, a two-font identity/reading split, and a rationed blue accent.

whatYouGet: A near-black chat color system where speaker identity comes from bubble-corner geometry rather than color-coding
Full specs for the asymmetric tucked-corner bubble pair, the character avatar gradient, the discover-grid card, and the italic roleplay-action text treatment
House rules protecting the single rationed accent blue and the two-font (identity vs. reading) typographic split that defines the brand
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer who specializes in conversational AI and companion-chat products, with a strong sense for how typographic and geometric restraint can make a chat surface feel immersive and book-like rather than app-like.

</role>
<reference_data>
Color roles: Canvas #0F0F10 (near-black, not pure black), Surface 1 #161618, AI Bubble #1C1C1F, User Bubble #26262A, Surface 2 #1E1E21, Divider #2A2A2E. The one rationed brand accent is Accent Blue #3A7BFD (pressed #2E63D6, soft tint #1B2A4A) — used only on the send button, primary CTAs, links, and the active tab, and never as a bubble fill. A secondary Lilac #9D7BFF exists solely as an alternate avatar-gradient stop, never as a control color. Text: Primary #ECECEE, Secondary #9A9AA2, Tertiary #66666E. Semantic: Success #4ED99A, Error #FF6B6B, Warning #FFB454.

Typography: a deliberate two-font system. Sora carries brand identity — wordmark, screen titles, character names, and all buttons. Inter carries reading comfort — every line of message text and every description, since AI replies can run long. Weight range across both faces is 400/500/600/700 only. Message text sits at 15pt/400 with a generous 1.5 line-height. Roleplay narration wrapped in asterisks renders in Inter 15pt italic at the Text Secondary color — this italic treatment is a signature, not a fallback style.

Spacing/radius: 4pt base scale (4/8/9/11/12/14/16/18/24/32/40/48/64). Bubble padding is 11pt vertical / 14pt horizontal, with a 12pt gap between message groups and 4pt within a same-speaker run. Radius scale: 4pt tuck corner, 8pt small affordances, 12pt search/sheet elements, 16pt discover cards, 18pt the three non-tucked bubble corners, 500pt (full pill) on every button and the composer, 50% circles on avatars and the send button.

Distinctive patterns: the asymmetric tucked-corner bubble — the AI bubble has one sharp 4pt corner (top-left) against three 18pt corners, and the user bubble mirrors it on the top-right, so speaker identity is legible from corner geometry alone rather than color; a radial-gradient circular character avatar (blue or lilac) as the single warm focal point on an otherwise neutral screen; a centered "greeting" title card (avatar + name + one-line description + persona's in-character first message) that opens every chat; a typing indicator built as three sequentially-dimming dots inside an AI-shaped (tucked-corner) bubble; a discover-grid character card bundling avatar, name, one-line hook, and a chat-count social-proof footer.
</reference_data>
<house_rules>
1. Speaker identity is signaled by the tucked corner geometry, never by a color difference — the AI and user bubble fills (#1C1C1F and #26262A) must stay close, calm greys, not a bright "user blue" vs. neutral AI split.
2. The accent blue (#3A7BFD) never fills a bubble under any circumstance — it is rationed to the send button, CTAs, links, and the active tab only, so it retains its meaning as "this is interactive."
3. Any span wrapped in asterisks (roleplay narration) must render in italic at the Text Secondary color — rendering it as plain upright body text destroys the speech-vs-narration distinction this product is built on.
4. Sora is reserved for identity elements (titles, names, buttons) and Inter for everything meant to be read at length — never set a paragraph of message text in Sora, since it lacks the reading comfort Inter provides over long AI replies.
5. The lilac gradient stop is an avatar-only decoration, never a second interactive UI color — introducing it on a button or tab would dilute the single-accent discipline.
6. Elevation stays essentially flat: the AI bubble's 1pt border is the only edge treatment in the entire chat surface, and drop shadows should not appear on bubbles or cards beyond that hairline.
7. Every chat opens with a centered greeting block (avatar, name, one-line description, in-character first message) before the conversation stream begins — this is a required structural beat, not decoration.
8. Streamed AI replies grow smoothly in height token-by-token with a blinking tail caret, and haptic feedback must stay silent during the stream itself to avoid a buzzing sensation.
9. Keep chrome minimal — a thin header and thin tab bar only; the message stream, not the surrounding UI, should dominate the screen at all times.
</house_rules>
<the_project>
- App/brand name: [your app name]
- Persona/character concept: [describe the kind of AI personas users chat with]
- Number of avatar gradient variants needed: [e.g. 2, or more]
- Whether roleplay-style narration is supported: [yes/no]
- Discovery/browse surface needed: [yes/no — grid of personas, etc.]
- Platform target: [iOS SwiftUI / React Native / Web]
- Light mode required: [yes/no]
- Existing brand constraints: [hex codes or "none"]
</the_project>
<what_to_give_me>
1. A full dark-first color token set (canvas, bubble fills, rationed accent, semantic states) with a one-line usage note per token.
2. A two-font typography ladder specifying exactly which roles use the identity face vs. the reading face, plus the roleplay-italic rule.
3. Full component specs for the AI bubble and user bubble pair, including exact corner-radius values per corner.
4. A spec for the character avatar (gradient recipe, size variants) and the greeting/title-card layout that opens a chat.
5. A discover-grid character card spec (avatar, name, description, chat-count footer) and the typing-indicator component.
6. A short do/don't list grounded in "identity via geometry not color" and "accent is rationed, never a bubble fill."
7. Three to five ready-to-paste SwiftUI (or your target framework) component snippets implementing the above.
</what_to_give_me>

name: ChatGPT Design System
summary: Radically minimal, monochromatic chat UI system centered on a circular black/white send button and bubble-free assistant text.
description: A production-grade prompt for building ChatGPT's post-2024 monochrome chat language: no accent color beyond a subtle link blue, bubble-free markdown responses, and the signature full-screen voice-mode sphere.

whatYouGet: A monochrome color system (pure white / charcoal-black canvas) with a single restrained link-blue accent and no brand color on chrome
Full specs for the circular inverse send button, the asymmetric user bubble, bubble-free markdown assistant responses, and the full-screen voice-mode sphere
House rules protecting the flat, shadow-free reading surface and the mandatory four-icon feedback row under every AI response
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in large-language-model chat interfaces, with a strong point of view on when a UI should recede entirely so that generated text can function as the primary interface.

</role>
<reference_data>
Color roles: Canvas #FFFFFF (light) / #212121 (dark, a charcoal rather than true black). Text Primary #0D0D0D / #ECECEC dark, Secondary #676767 / #B4B4B4 dark, Tertiary #8E8E8E / #707070 dark. The interface is deliberately near-monochrome — the only accent is Link Blue #2A7FFF, reserved for inline hyperlinks. The send button inverts by theme: black #0D0D0D circle in light mode, white #FFFFFF circle in dark mode, with the icon always the inverse of the circle color; disabled state is #CCCCCC / #4D4D4D. User message bubble: #F7F7F8 light / #2F2F2F dark — a soft gray barely distinct from canvas. Sidebar background is deliberately darker than canvas: #F9F9F9 light / #181818 dark. Code surfaces: inline chip #F0F0F0/#424242, block background #F7F7F8/#1E1E1E with a 1pt #E5E5E5/#363636 border. Voice-mode sphere gradient: #3B82F6 → #60A5FA → #93C5FD.

Typography: Söhne as the primary licensed face, falling back to Inter, then system SF Pro. Chat body sits at 16pt/400 with 1.5 line-height — pure document rhythm rather than UI rhythm. Markdown headings inside assistant responses step down from H1 24pt/600 to H2 20pt/600 to H3 17pt/600. Weight is concentrated at 400/500/600 only — no bold, no black, no thin. Code (inline and block) always renders in a true monospace (Menlo/SF Mono/IBM Plex Mono), never substituted.

Spacing/radius: 4pt base scale (4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/56/72). Message vertical gap between turns is 16pt. User bubble caps at 80% max-width and uses an asymmetric radius (18/18/18/4 — three rounded corners and one flat "pointer" corner). Radius scale: 4pt inline code, 8pt code blocks and tables, 12pt sheets, 24pt the compose-field wrapper, 50% circles for send/voice buttons and avatars.

Distinctive patterns: the assistant's response carries NO bubble at all — it is plain markdown-rendered text flowing down the page exactly like a document; a four-icon feedback row (regenerate, copy, thumbs-up, thumbs-down) appears below every assistant turn; a pill-shaped model-selector chip with a leading icon and trailing chevron sits top-left of the chat; the sidebar groups conversation history under time-based labels (Today / Yesterday / Previous 7 Days / Previous 30 Days / Month Year); voice mode is a full-screen takeover centered on a continuously pulsing, organically-deforming gradient sphere.
</reference_data>
<house_rules>
1. Assistant responses never get a bubble container — plain inline markdown flow is the rule, and wrapping the model's text in any kind of box or background contradicts the entire design intent.
2. The send button is always a circle, never a rounded rectangle or square, and its fill/icon colors must invert cleanly between light and dark (black-on-white, white-on-black) — no colored send button.
3. The UI stays monochromatic outside of the one restrained link blue (#2A7FFF) — do not introduce a brand accent color on chrome, buttons, or chips, and do not resurrect the legacy green as a control color.
4. The user bubble's asymmetric corner radius (18/18/18/4) is a deliberate "pointer" cue toward the sender — do not round all four corners equally.
5. Markdown rendering inside assistant responses must be fully realized: headings at their specified step sizes, syntax-highlighted code blocks with a copy affordance, and tables with bordered cells — a naive plain-text render of markdown syntax is a defect.
6. The four-icon feedback row (regenerate / copy / thumbs-up / thumbs-down) is mandatory below every assistant response — it is the signal that says "this is an AI answer, not a human message."
7. Shadows are reserved strictly for ephemeral, floating UI (sheets, pickers) — the chat surface itself, including code blocks and tables, stays perfectly flat and relies on borders, not elevation.
      
8. Text streams in character-by-character with no accompanying animation on the text itself — do not add fade-ins or slide effects per character, since the absence of motion is the correct pacing here.
9. Sidebar conversation history is always grouped by recency labels (Today/Yesterday/etc.), never rendered as one flat undifferentiated list.
</house_rules>
<the_project>
- App/brand name: [your app name]
- Primary use case: [general assistant / coding / customer support / other]
- Whether voice mode is in scope: [yes/no]
- Whether multiple selectable models exist: [yes/no, list them]
- Sidebar/history requirement: [yes/no]
- Platform target: [iOS SwiftUI / React Native / Web]
- Existing brand constraints: [hex codes or "none" — note the source app is deliberately near-colorless]
- Markdown feature set needed: [code, tables, LaTeX, images, etc.]
</the_project>
<what_to_give_me>
1. A full light + dark monochrome color token set with the single accent clearly marked as "link only."
2. A typography ladder from chat body through markdown H1-H3 to inline code, specifying the font fallback order.
3. Full specs for the send button (both theme states) and the user message bubble, including exact per-corner radius values.
4. A markdown-rendering spec for the assistant response area: headings, code blocks with copy button, tables, and the four-icon feedback row.
5. A model-selector chip spec and a time-grouped sidebar history spec.
6. If voice mode is in scope, a full spec for the full-screen gradient-sphere takeover including its pulse/deformation motion.
7. Three to five ready-to-paste SwiftUI (or your target framework) component snippets implementing the above.
</what_to_give_me>

name: Claude Design System
summary: Warm cream-paper chat system built on a serif/sans typographic asymmetry, Claude Orange, and an asterisk-star logomark.
description: A production-grade prompt for building Anthropic's Claude design language: a cream canvas, essayist serif assistant prose against sans user pills, and a single sacred orange accent.

whatYouGet: A warm cream-paper color system with a single sacred orange accent and warm-toned neutrals (never cool greys, never pure black)
Full specs for the flat assistant-message flow, the soft user-message pill, the artifact card, and the blinking streaming cursor
House rules protecting the serif/sans typographic role-asymmetry and the asterisk-star logomark that anchor the brand
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer with a background in editorial and publishing-grade typography, brought onto an AI assistant product to make its chat surface read like a warm, essayist document rather than a typical tech chat app.

</role>
<reference_data>
Color roles: Cream Paper #F8F4ED (primary canvas — the single most recognizable surface), Paper White #FBF9F4 (input fields, elevated surfaces), Surface Warm 1 #F0EAE0, Surface Warm 2 #E8E0D2, Divider Sand #DDD2BD. Text: Ink #2D2520 (warm near-black, never pure #000), Graphite Warm #5A4F44, Stone Warm #8A7E72, Bone Warm #B5AB9E. The single sacred accent is Claude Orange #D97757 (a desaturated terracotta, pressed #BE6242, soft tint #F2DDD0) — used only for the send button, the active model-chip state, the asterisk-star logomark, the streaming cursor, and links inside responses. Code-block palette runs warm-dark #1F1B16 background with syntax colors: keyword orange #D97757, string sage #7FB069, number gold #E8B96F, function periwinkle #9DA4F2. Dark mode keeps a warm near-black canvas #1F1B16 rather than a cool one.

Typography: a two-typeface system built around role, not just hierarchy. Tiempos Text (serif) carries every word of the assistant's message body and Tiempos Headline carries headings inside those responses; Styrene A (or Inter as substitute) carries user messages and all UI chrome. Assistant body sits at 16pt/400 with a notably loose 1.55 line-height — essay pacing, not chat pacing. JetBrains Mono handles code. Weight range: Tiempos 400/500/600/700, Styrene 400/500/700.

Spacing/radius: 4pt base scale up through 80pt. Standard margin is 20pt on iPhone, 32pt on iPad. Vertical gap between conversation turns is a generous 32pt with a faint divider. Radius scale: 4pt inline code, 10pt settings rows/action buttons, 12pt code blocks and artifact cards, 16pt the model-picker chip, 18pt the user-message pill, 20pt the chat input field, 24pt primary capsule CTAs, 50% circles for the send button and the logomark avatar.

Distinctive patterns: the assistant message has no bubble or container at all — just typography flowing across the cream canvas, led by a small asterisk-star logomark avatar; the user message sits in a soft rounded pill (not a bubble with a tail); a blinking orange caret (8pt wide, 18pt tall, 600ms blink interval) marks the trailing edge of an in-progress response; an artifact card slides out as a side pane on iPad or expands full-screen on iPhone when the model generates code, a document, or a chart; a "Thinking…" pill with a pulsing logomark appears before extended-thinking responses.
</reference_data>
<house_rules>
1. Assistant body text is always set in the serif (Tiempos), user messages always in the sans (Styrene/Inter) — this single typographic role-asymmetry is the defining brand decision and must never be collapsed into one typeface for both.
2. Claude Orange is sacred and rationed to five specific roles (send button, active model chip, logomark, streaming cursor, in-response links) — it must never appear as a body-text color, a heading color, or a section-divider fill.
3. Primary text color is a warm near-black ink (#2D2520), never pure #000000 — the warmth of the ink against the cream canvas is what makes the surface feel like paper rather than a screen.
4. Neither the user nor the assistant message uses a bubble with a tail — the assistant is a flat flow of type, and the user's turn is a soft pill with no pointer.
5. Code blocks live on a warm dark background (#1F1B16), never a blue-tinted dark — and syntax highlighting draws from the warm four-color set (orange/sage/gold/periwinkle), never a cool-toned syntax palette.
6. Assistant body line-height is fixed at 1.55 — tighter leading undermines the essayist, long-form reading experience this product is built around.
7. The asterisk-star logomark renders only in Claude Orange and is never substituted with a generic sparkle glyph or a stylized letter mark.
8. Streaming text appears word-by-word, not character-by-character — the pacing is deliberately calmer than a typewriter effect, and the orange caret blinks at a steady 600ms interval, pausing while a token is actively arriving.
9. There is no bottom tab bar anywhere in this product — navigation to conversation history happens exclusively through the sidebar, since the assistant is a single-purpose chat surface.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer fluent in Microsoft's Fluent Design System, tasked with building a consumer AI assistant that feels warm and physically layered rather than flat or enterprise-cold.

</role>
<reference_data>
Color roles: Canvas White #FFFFFF (light) / Dark Canvas #202020 (dark). Surface Acrylic #F3F3F3 / #2D2D2D dark — the frosted material used for answer cards, the prompt bar, chips, and the sidebar. Divider #E0E0E0 / #3A3A3A. Text Primary #242424 / #FFFFFF dark, Secondary #616161 / #A6A6A6 dark. Two accents divide responsibility: the Copilot Flourish Gradient (linear #FF6F61 coral → #FFB900 gold) fills the swirl logomark, the streaming shimmer, and the focused-input accent only; Fluent Blue #0078D4 (pressed #005A9E, tint #DEECF9) is the functional primary — active send button, links, selected toggle states. Semantic: Success #107C10/#6CCB5F dark, Warning #F7630C, Error #C50F1F/#FF99A4 dark.

Typography: Segoe UI (Inter as the open fallback), weights concentrated at 400/600/700 with no thin weight. Answer body sits at 16pt/400 with 1.5 line-height inside cards. Cascadia Code handles fenced code. Negative tracking (-0.2pt) applies only to the greeting/titles; body stays at 0pt tracking.

Spacing/radius: 4pt base scale (4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/56). Turn spacing is 16pt between a user turn and its answer, 24pt between full exchanges. Radius scale: 8pt for primary pill buttons and search fields (Fluent deliberately uses a softer rounded-rect rather than a full pill for primary actions), 12pt code blocks, 16pt answer cards and user turns (with a 4pt pointing corner), 18pt suggestion chips, 24pt the composer, 500pt (full pill) reserved specifically for the tone selector, 50% circles for avatars and send/voice buttons.

Distinctive patterns: Fluent acrylic — a frosted, tinted, blurred material (not a flat opaque fill) applied to the prompt bar, sidebar, sheets, and chips so content is faintly visible through them; a three-segment Creative/Balanced/Precise tone-selector pill that visibly reshapes the next answer's tone and accent intensity; conversational answers live inside soft rounded acrylic cards rather than as bare text; a streaming shimmer where a low-opacity flourish-gradient highlight sweeps the leading edge of text as it generates; navigation is sidebar-only, with no bottom tab bar anywhere in the product.
</reference_data>
<house_rules>
1. Every elevated surface (prompt bar, sidebar, sheets, chips) must be built as Fluent acrylic — a frosted, blurred, lightly tinted material — never a flat opaque panel; the layering is the material identity of this brand.
2. The flourish gradient (#FF6F61 → #FFB900) is rationed strictly to the logomark, the streaming shimmer, and the focus-emphasis accent — it must never fill a button, a flat panel background, or tint any body text.
3. Fluent Blue (#0078D4) owns every functional/interactive surface — the active send button, links, and selected toggle states — keeping a clean division of labor between "brand warmth" (flourish) and "function" (blue).
4. Answers always live inside a soft rounded acrylic card with a whisper shadow — never render assistant output as bare unboxed text, which is the opposite of this brand's signature.
5. Primary Fluent buttons use an 8pt rounded rectangle, not a full pill — reserve the full 500pt pill shape exclusively for the tone-selector control, which is this product's most distinctive component.
6. The Creative/Balanced/Precise tone selector must remain visible and consequential — selecting a tone should visibly shift the next answer's accent intensity, not just change an internal parameter invisibly.
7. There is no bottom tab bar — the sidebar is the sole primary navigation surface in this product.
8. Generation must feel alive: a streaming shimmer sweep plus a flourish-pulsing "thinking" indicator are required before and during every generated answer, never a static loading state.
9. Keep exact color parity for the flourish gradient stops between light and dark themes — do not let the warm accent drift or desaturate when the surface switches to dark.
</house_rules>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in research and reasoning-tool interfaces, brought in to design a chat surface whose core job is to make a model's step-by-step reasoning visible without letting it upstage the final answer.

</role>
<reference_data>
Color roles: Canvas #0E0E10 (dark) / #FFFFFF (light) — near-black, faintly cool. Surface 1 #1A1B1E, Surface 2 #232428, Surface 3 #2C2D31, Divider #2E2F33. The Reasoning BG is #16171A — deliberately darker than the canvas itself so the panel reads as receding behind the answer. The single accent is DeepSeek Blue #4D6BFE (pressed #3B57E0, soft tint #1E2240) used only for the whale logomark, the user bubble, the send button, active toggle borders/text, links, and citation chips — never for body text. Reasoning Text is a dimmed #8A8B90 (dark) / #6E6F74 (light), always rendered italic. Text Primary (the final answer) is #ECECEC (dark) / #1A1B1E (light), upright and full-contrast. Semantic: Success #2EBD85, Error/Stop #E5484D.

Typography: system sans (SF Pro / Inter fallback) with no custom display face — personality lives in the reasoning trace and the single blue, not the letterforms. Message body sits at 15pt/400 with 1.6 line-height; the reasoning trace sits smaller at 13pt/400 *italic* with 1.55 line-height. Weight range spans 400/500/600/700/800, with the italic-vs-upright distinction serving as the primary signal that trace and answer are different kinds of content.

Spacing/radius: 4pt base scale (4/8/10/12/16/18/24/32/48). Reasoning-panel internal padding is 12pt vertical / 14-16pt horizontal with a 10pt gap to the answer below it. Radius scale: 4pt inline code and the bubble's sender-pointing corner, 8pt code blocks, 10pt the reasoning panel and search bar, 18pt the user bubble's three rounded corners, 25pt the composer input pill, 999pt (full pill) on toggles/buttons/citation chips, 50% circles for send button and avatars.

Distinctive patterns: the reasoning-trace panel — a recessed, darker-than-canvas container with a 2pt solid-blue left bar, a "Thought for N seconds · tap to collapse" header, and chain-of-thought rendered in dimmed italic beneath it, collapsible to a single line; a paired DeepThink (R1) / Search toggle row above the composer, where an active toggle fills with a soft blue tint and blue border/text; the user bubble uses an asymmetric 18/18/4/18 corner radius (one flat corner pointing at the sender) while assistant replies have no bubble at all; inline `[n]` citation chips that appear only when Search is active.
</reference_data>
<house_rules>
1. The reasoning trace must always be visually subordinate to the answer — dimmer color, italic style, and a recessed (darker-than-canvas) background are all required simultaneously; rendering it upright or full-contrast breaks the core signal of the product.
2. The reasoning panel recedes by being darker than the canvas, not by casting a shadow — do not substitute a lighter "elevated card" treatment or a drop shadow for this recession effect.
3. DeepSeek Blue is the only accent in the entire product — do not introduce a second brand color, and never use it for body text; it is reserved for the logomark, user bubble, send button, active toggles, links, and citations.
4. Only the user gets a bubble (soft-blue fill, asymmetric 18/18/4/18 corner); assistant replies are always full-width with no bubble container.
5. The reasoning trace only appears when the DeepThink (R1) toggle is active — the fast model (V3) answers directly with no trace shown, and this distinction must never be blurred.
6. Both signature toggles (DeepThink and Search) use the identical soft-blue active treatment (tinted fill + blue border + blue text/icon) so their visual language reads as one consistent "mode is on" pattern.
7. The reasoning panel streams in token-by-token with a live-counting duration label before the final answer begins streaming — the two phases are sequential, never simultaneous.
8. Citation chips (`[n]`) only appear when Search is active, styled in monospace at the single accent color on a faint tinted pill — tapping one opens a source sheet.
9. The active tab bar item is signaled by accent-colored glyph and label only — never wrap it in a tinted pill background, since DeepSeek's chrome stays otherwise unaccented.
</house_rules>

</the_project>
<what_to_give_me>
1. A full dark + light color token set with the single accent's five permitted usage roles explicitly listed.
2. A typography ladder distinguishing the upright answer style from the italic reasoning-trace style, with exact sizes/weights/line-heights.
3. A full reasoning-trace panel spec: recessed background, left bar, header row, collapse/expand behavior, and streaming state.
4. A toggle-pill spec for the mode switches (e.g. DeepThink/Search), covering off/on states and the transition timing.
5. The user-bubble spec (asymmetric corner radius) and the assistant no-bubble layout with its header row.
6. A short do/don't list grounded in "trace is always subordinate, one accent only, recede via darkness not shadow."
7. Three to five ready-to-paste SwiftUI (or your target framework) component snippets implementing the above.
